subject.title: [Security] Missing audit trail and rate-limiting on sensitive plugin lifecycle hooks

question: Should trusted-operator plugin mutations gain a core durable audit event stream, and should any authenticated remote plugin-mutation surface also be rate-limited?
rationale: The proposal changes core security, actor-identity, and persistent-state contracts, while its suggested token bucket and mandatory user UUID do not fit all current lifecycle entry points.

options.title: Audit events only
options.body: Add durable structured mutation events while retaining unrestricted local operator CLI access.

options.title: Audit plus remote throttling
options.body: Add the shared audit contract and rate-limit only authenticated remote owner-command mutations at the gateway boundary.

options.title: Require exploit evidence
options.body: Keep current behavior until a concrete authorization bypass or operational abuse case demonstrates the need for core controls.

recommendation.title: Audit events only
recommendation.body: Add durable structured mutation events while retaining unrestricted local operator CLI access.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice changes the documented trusted-operator security boundary and plugin supply-chain policy.
